aiOverview.content: Used Ford models to avoid due to high repair costs and reliability issues include the 2012–2016 Focus (transmission failure), 2013–2014 Escape (engine issues), 2002–2005/2011–2013 Explorer (transmission/electrical), and 2015–2017 F-150. Focus on avoiding models with "PowerShift" transmissions and early EcoBoost engines. Key Ford Models and Years to Avoid Ford Focus (2012–2016): Often called "Avoid Like the Plague" due to severe PowerShift transmission shuddering, jerking, and failure, along with power steering issues. Ford Escape (2008, 2013–2014, 2020–2023): Older models suffer from engine/transmission failure, while newer models (2020+) face reliability complaints. Ford Explorer (2002–2005, 2011–2013): Known for severe transmission issues, suspension issues, and electrical problems. Ford F-150 (2004–2008, 2010, 2015–2017): Common engine and transmission failures, particularly with 5.4L Triton V8 and early EcoBoost engines. Ford Fiesta (2011–2016): Similar to the Focus, these are plagued by the automatic PowerShift transmission issues. Ford Edge (2015–2018): Known for significant mechanical issues and high maintenance costs. Ford Bronco Sport (2022): Identified by 24/7 Wall St. for issues with the fuel system and engine. Specific Reliability Issues PowerShift Transmission: The dry-clutch automatic transmission in 2011–2016 Fiestas and 2012–2016 Focus models is known for premature failure. EcoBoost Engines: Early versions of the 3.5L EcoBoost (2011-2017) and smaller turbo 3s/4s have had issues with high-pressure fueling and turbochargers. Engine Failure/Recall: Multiple models in the 2013–2014 era experienced high rates of engine issues, according to. What to Look For InsteadWhile certain years are problematic, later model years (2018+) of the Ford F-150, Explorer, and Escape have seen improvements. Generally, it is best to avoid older models with the PowerShift automatic and opt for manual transmission Focus/Fiestas, or trucks with naturally aspirated engines if looking at used models.
